title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This page belongs to the 'equation des lacets' notes that follow La Longue Marche. They are a hands-on construction of what is now the profinite Grothendieck-Teichmüller group.

The setting is as follows.
- pi_{0,3}^ is the free profinite group on two generators: the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,infinity}. It carries inertia ('lacet') generators l_0, l_1, l_infinity.
- Pi^+_{0,3} is its extension by S_3. Previous page, (37): it is generated by sigma_infinity and rho with sigma_infinity^2 = rho^3 = 1. So it is the profinite completion of Z/2 * Z/3, i.e. of PSL_2(Z). In that picture pi_{0,3} corresponds to the completion of Gamma(2)/±1 and S_3 = PSL_2(F_2).
- An automorphism u of Pi^+ inducing the identity on S_3 can be normalised so that u(sigma_infinity) = sigma_infinity and u(rho) = g rho, with g in pi_{0,3}^. The 3-torsion relation then forces (38): (g rho)^3 = 1, i.e. g rho(g) rho^2(g) = 1. This is the analogue of Drinfeld's hexagon (3-cycle) relation.
- The corollary ('Cor. Main') gives three equivalent conditions on u:
  (a) u(epsilon_0) is conjugate to epsilon_0^p, where epsilon_0 = l'_0 is a square root of l_0 lying over the transposition sigma_0; it corresponds to T = [[1,1],[0,1]] when l_0 corresponds to T^2.
  (b) u(l_0) is conjugate in pi_{0,3}^ to l_0^p.
  (c) u_0 = u restricted to pi_{0,3}^ respects the inertia structure, i.e. it sends each of l_0, l_1, l_infinity to a conjugate of a p-th power.

This page proves (b)⇒(c) and (c)⇒(a); (a)⇒(b) was proved on the previous page.

(b)⇒(c). By uniqueness of p in (b), write (39): u_0(l_0) = int(g_0)(l_0^p), with g_0 in pi_{0,3}^.
- Since u(rho) = g rho, we have u∘int(rho) = int(g)∘int(rho)∘u. Written as a relation on pi_{0,3}^: u_0 = int(g)∘rho∘u_0∘rho^{-1}.
- Using rho(l_0) = l_1: u_0(l_1) = int(g) rho(int(g_0) l_0^p) = int(g rho(g_0))(l_1^p). This is (40), with g_1 = g rho(g_0).
- Repeating: u_0(l_infinity) = int(g_infinity)(l_infinity^p), with g_infinity = g rho(g_1) = g rho(g) rho^2(g_0). This is (41).
- So inertia preservation at one puncture plus S_3-equivariance gives inertia preservation at all three punctures, with the same exponent p (the future cyclotomic exponent lambda).

(c)⇒(a). From u(epsilon_0)^2 = u_0(l_0) = int(g)(l_0^p) = (int(g) epsilon_0^p)^2, Grothendieck claims u(epsilon_0) = int(g)(epsilon_0^p). He reduces this to a uniqueness-of-square-root statement, marks 'vérifier' in the margin, and then writes 'OK'.

Purpose. The next page restricts to outer automorphisms of pi_{0,3}^ that respect the lacet structure and commute with S_3. It derives the parametrisation g = sigma_infinity(g_0) l_1^nu rho(g_0)^{-1}. This is Grothendieck's own route to the pairs (lambda, f) defining GT^, via automorphisms of PSL_2(Z)^ over S_3.
errors: The displayed relation 'rho u_0 rho^{-1} = int(g) u_0' has its sides swapped. The relation actually used on the next line, u_0(l_1) = int(g) rho u_0 rho^{-1}(l_1), is u_0 = int(g) rho u_0 rho^{-1}. That form is the one that follows from u(rho) = g rho. The computed results (40) and (41) are correct.

In (c)⇒(a) the uniqueness of square roots is only asserted ('vérifier ... OK'). A full argument goes like this. If x^2 = y^2 with y = int(g) epsilon_0^p, then (after conjugating) x commutes with l_0^p. One needs that the centralizer of l_0^p (p a unit) in PSL_2(Z)^ is the procyclic group generated by epsilon_0; this is a known but nontrivial fact about centralizers of inertia/parabolic elements in profinite completions. Then x = epsilon_0^a with 2a = 2p in Z^, and since Z^ is torsion-free, a = p. The page leaves this step unproved.
Wording: epsilon_0 is not an involution (its square is l_0, which has infinite order). The marginal word is therefore probably 'solution' or 'racine', not 'involution'.

ideas.what: Viewing the S_3-extension of the free profinite group of rank 2 as Z/2 * Z/3 profinite (PSL_2(Z)^) and studying its automorphisms inducing the identity on S_3; the relation (g rho)^3 = 1
ideas.modern_name: GT^ via automorphisms of B_3^/center = PSL_2(Z)^; 2-cycle and 3-cycle (hexagon) relations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara (1990-91); the PSL_2(Z) formulation is in Lochak-Schneps and Harbater-Schneps (1990s-2000)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only sketches the Teichmüller tower and GT idea; La Longue Marche (ed. Lochak-Schneps excerpts) unsure for this precise formulation

ideas.what: Inertia ('lacet') preservation at one puncture plus S_3-equivariance implies preservation at all three punctures with the same exponent p, with explicit conjugators g_1 = g rho(g_0), g_infinity = g rho(g) rho^2(g_0)
ideas.modern_name: Inertia-preserving (braid-like) outer automorphisms; cyclotomic exponent lambda in GT^

ideas.what: Equivalence of inertia conditions for l_0 and for its square root epsilon_0 (the order-2-lifted cusp element T); uniqueness of square roots via centralizers in PSL_2(Z)^
ideas.modern_name: Centralizers of parabolic/inertia elements in profinite completions

missed.claim: This is an early (circa 1981-84, before Drinfeld 1990) explicit derivation of the defining relations and inertia conditions of the profinite Grothendieck-Teichmüller group, done via automorphisms of PSL_2(Z)^ over S_3. That is the formulation later adopted by Lochak-Schneps. It documents Grothendieck's priority in detail, beyond what the Esquisse states, though the general priority is already acknowledged.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is of historical interest: it shows the PSL_2(Z)^ / S_3-equivariant formulation of GT^, with the cyclotomic exponent, in Grothendieck's own hand. Mathematically the content is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The page carries out a correct, pre-Drinfeld computation of the GT-type inertia conditions in the PSL_2(Z)^ model. The mathematics itself is now standard and Grothendieck's anticipation of GT is broadly known, so this is a modestly notable historical detail rather than a new result.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'Comme on sait l'unicité en p dans b)', not 'en g'.
The groups are written \hat\Pi_{0,3} (consistent with the previous page), and \hat\Pi^+_{0,3} in the last line.
The marginal word before 'de \hat\Pi^+_{0,3} de carré égal à ℓ_0' is probably 'solution' (or similar), not 'involution'; epsilon_0 is not an involution.
The left-margin word 'vérifier' annotates the last two lines, and 'OK' is written at the right.
